findings.problem: A text archive cap/write/sync error returned by detach_archive prevents finalize_recording even when the captured video is healthy. Live reception continues until stop, so failure can become visible only at finalization.
Manual recovery calls finalize_recording without a durable chat-completeness check. A later successful video retry can remove owned TS inputs without retaining a durable partial-chat warning.
Publishing a verified video clears the general job error. Chat preservation cannot rely on that transient error field.

Mutex/detach failure and successful detach with incomplete text storage currently share an Err path. Ignoring all errors would permit finalization while an archive may still be attached. Rich asset close already has a distinct warning/preserve-source path; its incomplete result must not be confused with complete text storage.
Removing the writer's128MiB cap alone would leave replay unable to read larger archives. Replay partial_file currently recognizes only a .part filename, not a truncated-but-valid JSONL archive.

decisions.separateOutcomes: Video validation, text-archive storage and optional rich-asset availability are different outcomes. A verified video with a durably recorded partial-chat warning may be played; it is not a claim that all requested recording data was saved.
decisions.noBlanketIgnore: Keep Result<ChatDetachOutcome, DetachFailure>. An inability to lock/take/detach the archive, or to prove its write target was closed, is a hard failure: do not publish completion or clean inputs. Once detached under the session lock, an archive cap/write/flush failure is a structured incomplete outcome, not a reason to skip independent video verification.
decisions.cleanup: Cleanup requires full video decode/hash verification, durable completed video proof, and affirmative durable text-storage completion with no existing preserve-source protection. Partial, unknown, writing, corrupt or unavailable chat status retains owned TS/merge inputs and all raw/normalized chat. Existing exact-owned cleanup restrictions remain; no glob-based ownership and no deletion of unknown files.
decisions.caps: Keep current raw-plus-normalized128MiB and all line/ring/reader/index limits. Rotation and long-file support require a separate writer/manifest/reader design and separate acceptance evidence; this batch neither removes nor increases those caps.
decisions.completionMeaning: A text-storage complete result means accepted archive writes were durably finished without a known local storage failure. It does not prove that an upstream disconnect lost no messages, every provider rich event was supported, timing is exact, or an empty/connection-only archive contains real chat. Do not display a blanket all-chat-saved claim.

detach.shape: Result<ChatDetachOutcome, DetachFailure>; outcome includes the detached archive identity and TextStorageOutcome, with existing asset-incomplete/preserve-source information kept separate.
detach.textOutcome: Complete or Partial with bounded typed reason codes (archive_limit, write_failed, flush_failed, interrupted, status_unknown). No raw error text, chat contents, author IDs, tokens or URLs in persisted diagnostics.
detach.fence: Take and close the current sink under its existing mutex before allowing a new recording attachment. An old finalizer must only use its detached job identity/outcome, never the current session's new archive. No additional media/chat receiver.
detach.writerStats: Keep bounded aggregate counts/byte totals and last-received sequence/time only if actually observed. Distinguish written/accepted from successfully synced values; do not label an unsynced counter as saved or invent a boundary after flush failure.

durableStatus.path: Owned job directory/chat-status.json is the immutable version1 writing/attachment marker; chat-status.final.json is the immutable version1 terminal proof. Both use exact basenames and a16KiB read bound. Windows pins all ancestors against rename/delete, holds an exclusive-write/delete temporary-file handle and publishes through same-handle FileRenameInfo with ReplaceIfExists=false. Unknown targets are never overwritten and no path-based temporary unlink occurs. Read/link/type/length/hash validation uses the actual held handle. Non-Windows no-replace fallback is not claimed Windows-equivalent verified security.
durableStatus.identity: Bind provider, job UUID and recording/attachment identity. Validate exact schema/version/enums, finite counters, owned regular file/ancestor identity and no reparse/hardlink access. Do not accept a renderer-provided path.
durableStatus.fields: Version/identity, storageState, bounded reason codes, whether originals must be retained, optional proven aggregate byte/sequence checkpoints. No text, nickname, raw account identifier, remote URL or credential.
durableStatus.begin: Persist the writing marker before the new recording is considered to have an attached writable archive. A failure prevents recording acceptance rather than silently creating an untracked successful archive.
durableStatus.finish: After actual detach and final flush attempts, durably publish complete/partial status before reporting a completed video. Use an owned temporary status file plus sync and verified publication; never overwrite an unknown target or discard the previous valid status on a failed update.
durableStatus.crash: Reader first validates the writing marker's identity/version, then the matching terminal proof. A valid partial terminal remains partial on every retry. A missing terminal after a writing marker becomes interrupted/partial on recovery. Legacy absence becomes unknown. Existing malformed, oversized, wrong-identity or conflicting terminal proof is fail-closed, not replaced or interpreted as complete. An interrupted temporary-file publication leaves the marker and original files intact; a corrupt published proof cannot be automatically repaired.
durableStatus.failure: If the required partial warning cannot be persisted, fail closed: preserve all inputs and any already-created/verified final video, retain the last valid journal, do not publish a completed library item, and surface/latch a persistence error. Existing ordinary-quit versus factory-reset shutdown_error rules apply; a timeout is not success.

dto.proposal: MediaLibraryItem.chatArchive?: { state: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'unknown'; reasons: string[]; originalsRetained: boolean } | null, using native allowlisted codes rather than arbitrary strings. A serde-default optional field maintains existing journal/IPC compatibility. The nested library entry in MediaJob exposes the same summary without adding job-state variants.
dto.semantics: completed still means verified playable video, while chatArchive.partial/unknown is an independent durable warning. Generic successful polling, publication error=None and retry must not clear it. Normal VOD downloads have no new chat claim.
dto.ui: Keep existing library/card/player geometry and interactions. Affected live recordings show a concise warning such as '채팅 일부 누락' or '채팅 상태 확인 필요', with a short reason and '원본 보존' where true. The same current item summary remains visible during replay; no long description, modal, unrelated action or fake progress is added.

flow: Create validated recording identity and durable writing marker; attach the archive only if initialization succeeds.
Maintain the existing single session receiver and bounded ring. A text cap or I/O failure remains sticky; it does not silently reset on later successful live messages or a new polling reply.
Stop this recording: detach its archive synchronously and fence late writes. Hard detach failure retains all data and fails the job.
For a safely detached archive, attempt final sync, classify local text storage, persist complete/partial proof and retain any existing rich-asset warning separately.

If proof is durable and video inputs are healthy, run the existing bounded merge/full decode/hash verification. Publish the verified video with its durable chat warning rather than treating chat failure as video corruption.

Clean exact-owned intermediates only when video proof and chat cleanup eligibility both succeed. Otherwise keep final video, source chunks, merge inputs, raw chat, normalized chat and status evidence.

Recovery/retry uses the same helper and cleanup gate, with no provider request or automatic new broadcast capture. Revalidate an already published media file; a retry cannot turn partial/unknown into complete merely because merge succeeds.
compatibility: Existing completed VOD and live files remain readable/playable with their original video proof. A missing optional legacy chat status is unknown/not recorded, never retroactively complete, and does not invalidate or rewrite existing media.
Do not bulk migrate or inspect user recordings. Read the small optional status only for the owned requested item as needed, with bounded I/O.
An unfinished legacy live recording lacking the new proof may be revalidated into a playable video with a durable unknown-status warning, but its original/intermediate cleanup remains disabled.

A corrupt/unreadable status for an existing completed video may show chat-state-unknown while verified video playback remains available. It must not authorize cleanup, source rewrite or a silent successful status repair.
Do not change old chat timestamps, backfill rich data, replace normalized/raw files, rewrite final media, or use missing actual messages as successful chat-preservation evidence.

approvedMinimalCorrection.recordedBeforeEdit: Parent approved after independently reading the official FILE_RENAME_INFO contract. The path buffer previously allocated offset(FileName)+path bytes, with only incidental alignment padding. Exact8-byte-aligned sizes leave no allocated UTF16 terminator, while first/second fixture directory names differ by one character. This is a concrete structural defect consistent with the observed intermittent invalid-name response.
approvedMinimalCorrection.decision: Allocate and pass an explicit additional WCHAR terminator; FileNameLength remains path bytes excluding NUL, dwBufferSize includes the terminator. Copy the same validated path and explicitly write NUL. Preserve same source handle, ancestor pins, no-replace and fail-closed checks. No retry or relaxed sharing/identity validation.
